items.text:
Your working directory is a checkout of the real downshift repository (the accessible dropdown/combobox primitive library) at the commit where the bug below reproduces. Find and fix the bug in the library source.

Bug: the `useSelect` hook supports character-key type-ahead search on its toggle button — the user types printable characters and the currently highlighted item jumps to the next item whose label starts with the characters typed so far (characters typed in quick succession accumulate into a single search query; if the user pauses, the next character starts a brand-new query). This has two bugs:

1. The Space character (`' '`) is not treated the same as other printable characters. Every other printable key gets appended to the in-progress search query, but Space is special-cased to instead toggle/select behavior (as if no search were active), even while the user is in the middle of typing a multi-character query that happens to contain a space. So typing a query like `1 2 3` — where the matching item's label literally contains spaces — does not work: as soon as the space character is typed, the search buffer is not extended the way it is for a letter or digit, and the wrong item ends up highlighted.

2. When continuing to add characters to an already-in-progress search query (i.e. the query so far is already 2 or more characters long), the search for the next matching item always starts scanning from one position *after* the currently highlighted item, unconditionally. That's correct for the very first character of a new query (you don't want to just re-match the item you're already on), but once a multi-character query is already in progress, the currently highlighted item itself is still a valid candidate — it may still match the longer query being typed, or it may be exactly the item that should be reached next. Always skipping past it means the search can land one item too far forward, or skip over an item that should have matched, so repeated/rapid-succession character searches don't reliably advance through all matching items in the order the user would expect.

Environment notes: dependencies are already installed (Node, npm). You can scope the existing Jest suite to whatever file you're iterating on with `npx kcd-scripts test --no-watch <path-to-file>`. Fix the library source; do not just add workarounds in test files.
I’ll trace the `useSelect` keydown/type-ahead path and its existing tests, then patch the source and run the narrow Jest test suite before checking the broader relevant tests.

items.text: The two defects are isolated: the toggle handler gives `' '` precedence over character handling, and `getItemIndexByCharacterKey` currently always applies the “start after highlight” offset despite the intended multi-character behavior already documented by its tests. I’m checking the test harness details now so the regression cases match the hook’s actual keyboard event flow.

The existing utility test explicitly requires inclusive scanning for queries longer than one character, so the source is failing its own intended contract. I’ll fix the scan start with a `highlightedIndex >= 0` guard, and route Space to character search only when `inputValue` is already non-empty; otherwise its established open/select behavior remains unchanged.

items.text:
Fixed both `useSelect` type-ahead bugs:

- Space now extends an active search query while preserving normal toggle/select behavior otherwise.
- Multi-character searches now include the currently highlighted item when scanning.
- Added regression coverage for queries like `1 2 3`.

Verified: all 8 `useSelect` test suites pass, 212 tests total.
